learningObjective: Diagnose a scenario in which torch.compile recompiles repeatedly and identify the correct remediation approach.

canonicalClaims.claim: When a Python scalar attribute reachable to Dynamo changes between calls, Dynamo specializes on its observed value and produces a fresh compile whenever it changes; the correct remediation is to pass the varying value as a tensor input (or otherwise force dynamic treatment) so it becomes a graph input rather than a specialization key.
conditions: The API can accept the varying scalar as an input.
nonImplications: Does not imply every Python-scalar guard is removable; some ops still specialize.
Does not imply the fix eliminates all recompiles.

misconceptions.whyWrong: It hides the symptom but the recompile cost per new value is still paid.
reduce-overhead focuses on CUDA Graph capture and dispatch overhead; it does not disable guards.

misconceptions.claim: Underscore-prefixed attributes are skipped by Dynamo guards.
TorchDynamo never guards Python attributes on user classes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Dynamo does install guards on attributes it can inspect on the traced object.

implementationFacts: Python-scalar attributes on nn.Module become guards during tracing
Passing scalars as tensors makes them graph inputs, avoiding specialization
performanceScenarios: Fixing scalar-guard thrashing is one of the highest-value torch.compile tuning steps in production training loops.
